commercial_incentive: Channel name (Admitium) suggests a consulting brand, but no explicit sales pitch in this transcript
key_insights: New Stanford AOs are each assigned a geographic territory (e.g. part of California, Northeast, Australia/NZ) and read all applicants from those regions
Before the season starts, all officers calibrate together by reading sample files to agree on what an admit, waitlist, and deny look like
Officers use a written 'admission officer handbook' with rating categories (e.g. test scores, curriculum rigor) applied consistently to every file
Reading order is transcript first, then activities list, essays, letters of support, and interview report, before assigning ratings
Write-up time varies hugely: a likely-deny gets ~10 minutes, but a file the reader wants to advocate for can take up to 40 minutes
The reader writes a persuasive summary/talking points at read time specifically to use months later in committee, since details fade from memory
In committee, other officers only see assigned ratings (via spreadsheet), not the actual application, so the reading officer must orally pitch the candidate
Admission is decided by committee vote after the original reader advocates for roughly 30 seconds against colleagues who read other regional applicant pools
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speaker (former Stanford AO) says a quick deny write-up takes about 10 minutes; an advocated file can take up to 40 minutes
Speaker describes committee groups of roughly 10 colleagues voting on admits
notable_or_distinctive: Gives a rare procedural walkthrough of the internal Stanford reading and committee-vote mechanics from a former AO's first-person account, rather than generic application tips.
reliability_notes: Single anecdotal account from one self-identified former Stanford AO; process details (handbook, committee format) may have changed or varied by year and cannot be independently verified from the transcript alone.
